html:
The Monte Carlo Casino opened in 1863 under Prince Charles III, who needed money after Monaco lost most of its land in 1861. It made the principality rich.

The French businessman François Blanc ran it and the new railway from Nice brought gamblers. The district around it was named Monte Carlo after the prince in 1866. Its gaming rooms were later designed by Charles Garnier, architect of the Paris Opera. Monégasques themselves were barred from gambling.

The profits were so large that Monaco abolished income tax for its residents in 1869, which drew the wealthy ever since. The casino helped make the Riviera a playground of Europe's rich, and gave the Grimaldi state its later fame, with the Grand Prix and Princess Grace.
